title: SDE: A Simplified and Disentangled Dependency Encoding Framework for State Space Models in Time Series Forecasting

problem.claim: Long-term time series forecasting models struggle to capture complex and structured temporal and cross-variate dependencies.

gap.claim: Existing approaches often treat dependencies in isolation, while excessive nonlinearity in conventional state space models can introduce redundancy for semantically sparse time series.

contributions.claim: The authors propose SDE, a simplified and disentangled dependency encoding framework for state space models in long-term time series forecasting.

SDE removes unnecessary nonlinearities from vanilla state space models and introduces disentangled encoding to model cross-variate dependencies while reducing interference between temporal and feature dimensions.
The authors provide theoretical justifications for the framework's design choices.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe SDE as a novel framework for enhancing state space models in long-term time series forecasting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on nine real-world benchmark datasets reportedly show that SDE-enhanced state space models consistently outperform state-of-the-art time series forecasting models.
The authors report that their code is available in a public repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep learning has produced many models for long-term time series forecasting.
Existing methods have difficulty capturing structured dependencies, and isolated or excessive nonlinear processing can add noise or redundancy.
The authors investigate state space models because of their potential advantages for representing the identified dependencies.
SDE simplifies state space models and disentangles temporal and feature dependency encoding.
The authors report theoretical support and benchmark results favoring the proposed design.

source_observation.claim: The abstract distinguishes order, semantic, and cross-variate dependencies and reports that treating them in isolation can introduce noise.

interpretation.claim: Forecasting architectures may benefit from explicitly representing dependency types and managing their interactions.

application.claim: When designing multivariate forecasting models, consider separate mechanisms for temporal and cross-feature dependencies with controlled interaction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this separation benefits datasets whose dependency structure differs from the reported benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: The authors report that excessive nonlinearity in conventional state space models introduces redundancy for semantically sparse time series.

interpretation.claim: Reducing model nonlinearity may improve suitability when the data contain sparse semantic structure.

application.claim: For semantically sparse forecasting data, evaluate whether simplifying nonlinear components removes redundancy without reducing predictive capacity.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which forms of nonlinearity are redundant or when simplification may be harmful.

unknowns: The abstract does not report quantitative performance values, baselines, or dataset names.
The abstract does not describe the theoretical results or their assumptions.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or ablation results.
